hott.already_proved: Arsiwalla-Gorard(-Elshatlawy) already own the "transitions as paths, rewriting systems as homotopy types" framing: multiway (nondeterministic) rewriting systems with order-n homotopies form n-fold categories whose limit is an infinity-groupoid. Crucially, the higher structure there comes from nondeterministic branching plus homotopies induced by rule inclusion in rulial space; a deterministic ECA trajectory is a single path, the degenerate case with no higher cells. Kraus-von Raumer proved the induction principle for path spaces of coequalizers/pushouts (the exact tool for computing loop spaces of transition-graph HITs) and showed such path spaces reduce to combinatorial rewriting/confluence data, i.e., the homotopy machinery hands back the combinatorics you started with. Silvasi-Tomasek formalized computable CA over bounded grids in Lean, confirming that plain type-theoretic formalization of CA is routine and touches none of the mathematics. Standard HoTT (Book Thm 7.1.9 + funext): Bool is an hSet, so configurations Z->Bool and the center column N->Bool are hSets; all their identity types are mere propositions and all loop spaces are contractible.
hott.candidate_first_experiment: An afternoon Agda/Lean exercise, not a Python run: (1) prove the center-column type N->Bool is an hSet and hence that any "P1 as loop-space" statement is propositionally equal to the plain first-order proposition; (2) define the trajectory HIT (point per configuration, path per step) and prove its loop space at the initial configuration is equivalent to "the orbit contains a cycle", then prove that false in one line from support growth. Both halves succeed and thereby kill the arm; there is nothing left to run.

nsa.already_proved: Conservativity: NSA proves no standard statement beyond ZFC's reach (Nelson 1977), so hyperfinite runs per se add zero deductive power; P1/P2/P3 are standard arithmetic statements. Textbook NSA gives exact quantifier-level equivalences: lim d_N = 1/2 iff st(d_N) = 1/2 for EVERY infinite hypernatural N, and eventual p-periodicity iff *a(t+p) = *a(t) for all infinite t (overspill); these are restatements, not reductions. Kamae 1982 proved the Loeb/hyperfinite-cyclic machinery delivers a.e. ergodic theorems; Jin 2002 and the Di Nasso-Goldbring-Lupini corpus proved it delivers new theorems about positive-density sets under translation invariance. Settled background: Rule 30 is surjective, so uniform Bernoulli is invariant, and a.e.-flavored density-1/2 results for random initial conditions already exist standardly; the single-black-cell configuration is a measure-zero point those results cannot see. Jen 1990/Kopra 2023 settle width-two aperiodicity; width one (the prize) is open with no NSA content anywhere in the line.
nsa.open_gap: Literally unoccupied square: no published work applies nonstandard analysis (hyperfinite time/rows, overspill, Loeb measure) to any orbit-level statement about a specific cellular automaton, Rule 30 included; searches for the intersection return nothing, and the only model-theory-on-CA paper (Baldwin-Shelah 2000) is about classification formalization. The precise candidate instantiation would be: a Kamae-style hyperfinite-cyclic representation of the subshift generated by the center column, with a Loeb-measure identification of a shift-invariant measure on it whose density of 1s is 1/2 and which is the UNIQUE invariant measure (unique ergodicity would standardly imply P2). But the gap is unoccupied for cause: existence of an invariant measure is trivial (Krylov-Bogolyubov), and the NSA machinery contributes nothing toward uniqueness, which is a rule-specific combinatorial fact of the same difficulty class as P2 itself.
nsa.proof_relevance: In principle (via conservativity) a completed Loeb-measure argument would yield the standard theorem for P2: lim_{N to infinity} (1/N)|{t < N : a(t) = 1}| = 1/2 for the center column a(t) from the single-1 initial condition, obtained as st(Loeb-density) = 1/2 at every infinite hyperfinite horizon N. For P1 the overspill form is: for every standard p there exists an infinite t with *a(t+p) not equal to *a(t). Both are exact logical restatements of the targets, so the technique names the formal statements but supplies no independent route to them; for P3 (complexity lower bound): none plausible, NSA has no purchase on computational effort.
nsa.feasibility: Nothing meaningful is runnable: NSA is pure proof machinery with no computable content here. The only concrete shadow, simulating Rule 30 on cyclic rows Z/NZ as finite avatars of hyperfinite rows, is vacuous by locality: the cyclic center column agrees exactly with the infinite-lattice column for t below roughly N/2, so truncation experiments reproduce the known column bit-for-bit, and any density statistics gathered are statistical evidence, which counts as no path. A minutes-long Python check of the agreement window is the entire runnable surface; an overnight budget buys nothing more.

nsa.verdict_rationale: Two independent closures. First, conservativity (Nelson 1977): hyperfinite runs, transfer, and overspill cannot produce a standard theorem lacking a standard proof, and the NSA reformulations of P1/P2 are definitional restatements (all-infinite-N quantification is the limit; galaxy periodicity is eventual periodicity), so the technique's framing adds zero leverage by itself. Second, the only mode in which NSA has historically produced new theorems, Loeb-measure averaging (Kamae 1982; Jin 2002; DGL 2019), outputs a.e./positive-density conclusions that require invariance or amenability structure and are constitutionally blind to a single measure-zero orbit, which is exactly the known standard obstruction separating 'a.e. initial condition has density 1/2' from P2. Any NSA derivation that closed the gap would have to consume a rule-specific combinatorial input (e.g., unique ergodicity of the column subshift) that itself constitutes the standard proof. No prior NSA-on-CA work exists to extend, and the unoccupied gap is unoccupied for this structural reason, not neglect.

quantum.already_proved: The encoding step is routine, not research: any ECA cell update compiles to CNOTs plus one Toffoli-class gate (Rule 30's p XOR q XOR r XOR qr is degree 2, hence non-Clifford; course-level demos already run ECAs on quantum hardware with 3 Toffolis + 1 ancilla). For the LINEAR rules the whole program is finished: Gutschow-Uphoff-Werner-Zimboras 2010 classify Clifford QCA dynamics (periodic/fractal/glider) and prove exact linear entanglement-growth asymptotics; Rule 30 sits outside that classification precisely because it is nonlinear. For the class that DOES contain any reversible embedding of Rule 30 (permutation/"automaton" circuits), Iaconis 2021 proves the two facts that gut this technique: (i) computational basis states evolve to computational basis states, so the single-black-cell prize trajectory has exactly zero entanglement across every cut at every t and stabilizer rank 1; (ii) on superposed inputs these circuits generate volume-law entanglement with GUE entanglement-spectrum statistics while remaining efficiently classically simulable for computational-basis sampling, so entanglement growth is provably not a hardness certificate for this circuit family. The descriptive program for classical ECAs is also already published: Merbis-Bakker 2024 define operator entanglement entropy of the CA transition MPO, compute it for ECAs explicitly including Rule 30, and use its growth to classify Wolfram classes (noting Rule 30's OE curve is boundary-condition sensitive: open boundaries push it into their Type II.B despite chaos). Hillberry et al. 2021 did the entanglement/complexity survey for quantized ECA-like rules. On the lower-bound side: best stabilizer-rank lower bound for n magic states is Omega(n) (Peleg-Shpilka-Volk 2022); best explicit general-circuit lower bound is 3.1n - o(n) (Li-Yang STOC 2022).
quantum.candidate_first_experiment: Bennett-embed Rule 30 (per cell: 2 CNOTs + 1 Toffoli writing p XOR q XOR r XOR qr to a fresh ancilla layer) on a 2t+1-cell light cone, t = 10-12, numpy statevector (~25 qubits, 512 MB). Evolve (a) the single-black-cell basis state and (b) the uniform superposition over initial conditions; record center-cut von Neumann entropy vs t against Rule 90/150 Clifford controls and reproduce the Merbis-Bakker MPO operator-entanglement curve for Rule 30 as a cross-check. Run (a) first: it costs an afternoon and is the disconfirming test, since it will read exactly 0.0 at every step, exhibiting on real hardware-scale data that the proposed observable is blind to the prize trajectory.

quantum.open_gap: The only genuinely unproved statement in reach is an exact asymptotic for the operator entanglement entropy of Rule 30's transition-matrix MPO (Merbis-Bakker's curves are numerical, and their Rule 30 result is boundary-condition dependent). A referee would grant that as open. But it is a statement about the ensemble action of the global rule on all configurations, and it is provably disconnected from the prize object: the single-black-cell orbit is one computational basis vector, on which every entanglement/magic/stabilizer-rank monotone of the permutation unitary evaluates trivially (entropy 0, rank 1) at all times. No published work derives, or proposes a route to, any center-column statement from a quantum encoding, and Iaconis 2021 supplies the in-principle obstruction rather than a mere absence: this circuit class combines maximal entanglement with efficient classical simulability, so no entanglement-to-hardness transfer exists to be found.
quantum.proof_relevance: None plausible. For P1/P2: the quantities this technique produces (cut entropies, operator entanglement, magic monotones) are either identically trivial on the single-seed trajectory or are ensemble averages over all initial conditions; neither can express 'the center column is not eventually periodic' or 'the density of 1s is 1/2', which are statements about one specific orbit. For P3: a transfer would require an unconditional lower bound on ALL classical computation of cell(t), i.e., a 2^{Omega(n)} explicit lower bound at input size n = log t; entanglement growth provably cannot supply it (automaton circuits are classically simulable at maximal entanglement, Iaconis 2021), stabilizer-rank technology tops out at Omega(n) (Peleg-Shpilka-Volk 2022), and explicit circuit lower bounds top out at 3.1n (Li-Yang 2022), with the natural-proofs and relativization barriers standing between here and there.

Not runnable: exact stabilizer-rank computation beyond ~6-8 qubits (combinatorial search over stabilizer dictionaries), anything probing asymptotic growth, and of course any lower bound. Everything runnable yields curves that reproduce published phenomenology; under the panel's own ground rule, none of it advances a formal statement.

quantum.verdict_rationale: Three independent dooms, each sufficient. (1) Degeneracy on the object of study: any reversible embedding of Rule 30 is a permutation circuit, and the prize trajectory is a computational basis state, so the proposed observable, entanglement across the center cut, is identically zero for all t on the only orbit P1-P3 ask about; nonzero values require superposed inputs, which convert every result into an ensemble statement about all initial conditions. (2) The hardness arrow is severed in principle, not just unproven: Iaconis (PRX Quantum 2021) shows exactly this circuit class produces volume-law entanglement with chaotic (GUE) entanglement spectra while remaining efficiently classically simulable for computational-basis sampling, so no entanglement or operator-spreading measurement can ever certify the computational irreducibility P3 demands. (3) The lower-bound technology gap is categorical: P3 as circuit complexity is a 2^{Omega(n)} explicit lower bound at n = log t input bits, while the field's frontier is 3.1n for circuits and Omega(n) for stabilizer rank. Meanwhile the salvageable descriptive content (entanglement/OE phenomenology of quantized ECAs including Rule 30 specifically) is already published by Merbis-Bakker 2024, Hillberry et al. 2021, and, for the linear case with full rigor, Gutschow et al. 2010. There is no unoccupied gap that connects to the center column.
quantum.kill_condition_sketch: Two-stage kill, and stage one fires on paper: (a) the single-black-cell input yields center-cut entropy 0.000 at every step (guaranteed for a permutation circuit on a basis state), confirming the observable cannot see the prize orbit; the arm survives only by retreating to superposed inputs. (b) For superposed inputs, kill if Rule 30's center-cut entropy curve is indistinguishable in functional form (linear ramp to saturation, same slope class within seed-to-seed variance over 20+ random product-basis inputs) from the Clifford Rule 90/150 controls, i.e., the measurement does not even separate nonlinear from linear rules, let alone bear on the center column; and kill independently if artificially scrambling the center column of the classical trajectory (surgery on the embedded history ancillas) leaves every measured entanglement/magic curve unchanged, proving the observables are insensitive to the object P1-P3 concern.

latent.already_proved: The learned-representation half is occupied: Gilpin (PRE 2019) shows every CA is exactly representable as a small CNN and analyzes trained-network representations across ECA rules; Burtsev (NeurIPS'24 MATH-AI workshop) probes transformer internal representations of ECA dynamics including chaotic rules; Taga-Kato-Kawahara-Yamazaki-Nakao (Chaos 2021) execute the linear-latent-embedding program for ECA via Koopman one-hot lifting and explicitly derive conserved quantities from unit-circle eigenvalues on finite periodic lattices. The formal-target half is settled negatively for Rule 30: Baird-Fagin (Automata 2010, verified verbatim from the PDF, Fig. 2 caption and Fig. 5 legend) prove Rule 30 has NO nontrivial additive conserved energy function at ANY window size (extending Hattori-Takesue 1991, who gave the necessary-and-sufficient condition and classified ECA invariants); Kleveland (Proc. AMS 1997) proves leftmost-permutive CA (Rule 30 is left-permutive) are strongly mixing w.r.t. uniform Bernoulli measure, which by standard ergodic theory kills all non-constant measurable invariant observables and all non-constant Koopman eigenfunctions on L2(uniform). So the two natural formalizations of a latent-space conserved coordinate or continuous symmetry, additive local invariants and measure-level invariants/eigenfunctions, are both provably empty; any conserved-looking latent direction is necessarily a trivial (Baird-Fagin's complete trivial theory), a finite-size/boundary artifact, or an object outside the linear-additive and L2 classes.
latent.candidate_first_experiment: No training first. tda.already_proved: Nothing about Rule 30. The prior line establishes only empirical facts: Betti-number time series of spatiotemporal fields distinguish chaotic from ordered regimes (Gameiro-Kalies-Mischaikow 2004); TDA descriptors separate Wolfram's four ECA classes in one non-peer-reviewed 2025 preprint (which filters state space, not the spacetime diagram); persistence summaries quantify CA-generated biological patterns (Cleveland et al. 2022). No theorem anywhere links a persistence invariant of any CA spacetime diagram to a symbolic property (eventual periodicity, density, computational cost) of a single column. Separately, the descriptive content that spacetime-diagram persistence would capture for Rule 30, the enclosed white triangles and their size distribution, has been known informally since NKS (pp. 27-29), also only empirically.
tda.open_gap: Literally unoccupied: no published or preprint work computes persistent homology of the Rule 30 single-seed spacetime diagram, and no theorem of the form 'column eventually periodic implies some persistence invariant of the diagram is eventually periodic/degenerate' exists for any CA (verified by two arXiv API sweeps and three targeted web searches this session). A referee would confirm novelty of the application. But the gap is unoccupied for a structural reason: (i) under the natural grow-by-rows filtration, every H1 bar of the black cubical complex corresponds bijectively to one enclosed white triangle (Rule 30's white-run dynamics are locally forced: interior (0,0,0)->0, right flank always closes), born at its enclosing row and immortal, so the persistence diagram is a lossy re-encoding of white-triangle bookkeeping; (ii) the diagram near the center is determined by columns 0 AND 1 jointly (left-permutivity), and Jen 1990 Prop 3 / Kopra TCS 2023 show adjacent columns cannot both be eventually periodic, so periodicity of column 0 alone forces no periodicity of any neighborhood of the point cloud, hence no homological consequence.
tda.proof_relevance: None plausible. The only candidate formal statement is: 'if the center column is eventually periodic (P1 negation), then the sequence of persistence diagrams of the time-filtered cubical complex restricted to a width-w centered band is eventually periodic in t.' That implication is false as stated, because the band's contents are a function of columns 0 and 1 jointly, not of column 0; repairing it requires assuming joint band periodicity, which collapses the approach into Rowland-style column-band arguments (off-limits here) with persistence as a strictly lossy summary of the band's symbolic contents, adding zero leverage. For P2, the density of 1s in the center column is an H0-level count on a width-1 subcomplex, a trivial re-encoding with no TDA content. For P3, persistence is computed FROM the completed diagram, so it cannot lower-bound the cost of computing the diagram; no link exists even in principle.
tda.feasibility: Runnable overnight: single-seed evolution to t about 2-3x10^4 rows (10^8-10^9 cells) in numpy; H1 persistence via direct white-triangle enumeration in O(cells) (the bijection makes cubical PH software unnecessary, but GUDHI's cubical complex handles band windows of width <= 64 to t=10^5 easily); Betti curves and persistence-diagram sequences for centered bands; fiber-pair comparisons across random finite ICs sharing a center-column prefix. Not runnable/pointless: Vietoris-Rips on millions of points (quadratic blowup), and no amount of compute converts Betti curves into a formal statement, per the ground rule that statistical observation counts as no path.
tda.repo_overlap: No direct overlap: no repo ARM works on TDA/homology. But the sole formalization route (persistence of a centered band being eventually periodic) degenerates into centered-band periodicity claims, which is exactly the off-limits 'Rowland-style column-band lock proofs' territory; any attempt to salvage this arm as a proof vehicle collides with that reservation while contributing only a lossy summary of data those arms already handle symbolically.
tda.verdict_rationale: Closed not because prior work occupies the gap (it does not; all TDA-on-CA work is empirical classification, and none touches Rule 30) but because the direction is structurally doomed for all three prize questions. The time-filtration persistence diagram of the spacetime cloud is equivalent data to enclosed-white-triangle bookkeeping, a descriptive statistic known since NKS with no theorem attached; center-column periodicity constrains no spatial neighborhood of the diagram (columns 0 and 1 jointly determine the right half, and Jen/Kopra prove they cannot both be periodic), so no persistence invariant can be a function of the center column without importing off-limits joint-band hypotheses; and persistence computed from the diagram is definitionally irrelevant to P3 lower bounds. Under the panel's ground rule that empirical/statistical observation counts as no path, a technique whose entire output is descriptive statistics with a provably absent bridge to the target column is dead on arrival.
tda.candidate_first_experiment: Two-hour numpy test, no PH library needed for part (a): (a) evolve the single seed to t=2^12, compute the grow-by-rows cubical H1 barcode (GUDHI) and independently enumerate enclosed white triangles with their closing rows; verify the predicted bijection (bar birth = enclosure row, all bars immortal). (b) Sample random finite-support ICs, collect pairs whose center columns agree on the first n=64 symbols but whose columns 1..15 differ; compute persistence diagrams of the width-16 centered band for each; measure bottleneck distance within pairs vs across pairs. If within-pair distances are statistically indistinguishable from across-pair distances, no persistent invariant of the band carries center-column information beyond what the raw symbols already carry.
tda.kill_condition_sketch: Kill fires if EITHER (a) the H1-bar-to-white-triangle bijection holds exactly at all tested t (persistence adds zero information beyond known triangle statistics), OR (b) centered-band persistence diagrams vary freely across diagrams sharing a long center-column prefix (no persistence functional is even approximately a function of the center column). Both are the expected outcomes on structural grounds, so this kill condition fires on the plausible negative; the arm survives only if some persistence functional is empirically invariant across same-center-column diagrams, and even that survival would be a symbolic-dynamics fact about bands (off-limits territory), not a TDA contribution.

axiomatic.already_proved: Linear CA columns from eventually periodic seeds are exactly the p-automatic sequences (Litow-Dumas + Rowland-Yassawi 2015), and by Büchi-Bruyère 1994 these are exactly the sets FO-definable in (N,+,V_p); for such columns eventual periodicity is decidable (Honkala 1986) and the t-th term is computable in O(log t) DFA steps. Nonlinear CA columns can be nonautomatic, but only via purpose-built automata (Marcovici-Stoll-Tahay 2018); no criterion exists for a GIVEN nonlinear CA. The FO theory of any CA's phase space (one-step relation) is decidable via omega-automatic presentations (Sutner; Finkel 2011), and the MSO-model view of grids is worked out at the level of subshift classes (Jeandel-Theyssier 2013); iterated-time/orbit predicates fall outside the decidable fragment. On the Rule 30 side, width-2 trace aperiodicity is proved and width-1 is explicitly open (Jen 1990; Kopra 2023 Problem 3.10). Standard facts: eventually periodic implies k-automatic for every k; 2-automatic implies factor complexity O(n) and implies the Christol algebraicity of the generating function over F_2.
axiomatic.open_gap: Nobody has posed, attacked, or even empirically measured automaticity of the Rule 30 center column. Checkable absences: (a) export.arxiv.org full-text query for "Rule 30" AND "automatic sequence" returns zero papers (verified 2026-08-30); (b) the Allouche-Shallit-Yassawi non-automaticity survey never mentions Rule 30 (full-text verified); (c) OEIS A051023 carries no comment on automaticity, algebraicity, or kernels; (d) no published computation of the column's 2-kernel growth or Myhill-Nerode DFA lower bounds exists. The unexplored statement is the definability dichotomy itself: {t : c(t)=1} is FO-definable in (N,+,V_2) iff c is 2-automatic; EITHER branch has prize consequences (see proof_relevance), yet neither branch has a single published partial result for Rule 30. Secondary unexplored piece: whether the one-seed spacetime structure (N x Z, successors, black-cell predicate) admits an automatic presentation, which would force the column automatic, and where its FO theory sits relative to the Sutner-Finkel decidable phase-space fragment.
axiomatic.proof_relevance: Target theorem: "A051023 is not 2-automatic", equivalently (Christol) "the generating function of the center column in F_2[[x]] is transcendental over F_2(x)", equivalently (Büchi-Bruyère) "{t : c(t)=1} is not FO-definable in (N,+,V_2)". Since every eventually periodic sequence is k-automatic for every k>=2, this theorem implies P1. Converse branch: a proof of 2-automaticity would give an O(log t) DFA algorithm for the t-th center bit, refuting the P3 conjecture, and would make P1 a finite computation (Honkala 1986) and letter frequencies effectively analyzable (P2). Honest caveat: non-automaticity is strictly STRONGER than P1 (P1 does not imply it), so this is a steeper target justified only by its different toolbox (kernel finiteness, Christol algebraicity, definability, closure properties), not a shortcut.
axiomatic.feasibility: Runnable overnight in Python/numpy on one Apple Silicon Mac: center column to N ~ 2^21 bits via bit-packed row evolution (~10^12 word-ops, well under a night; Wolfram's prize materials also distribute precomputed center-column bits); truncated 2-kernel census (distinct 256-bit fingerprints of subsequences c(2^i n + j) for i <= ~18); Myhill-Nerode minimal-DFA state lower bounds from the truncated kernel; factor complexity p(n) for n <= ~30 via suffix automaton; Rule 90/150 columns as positive automatic controls (kernels must saturate, validating the probe) and a seeded random column as negative control. NOT runnable: deciding automaticity from data (undecidable in general), FO-theory proof search, or synthesizing a 2D automatic presentation. Note ARM7's quadtree-DAG counts already constitute unframed empirical evidence against 2-automaticity of the full 2D diagram (bounded 2D kernel would force O(log n) DAG nodes; measured 3,704 at n=512 with rising exponent ~1.48), but the 1D column kernel is a separate, much cheaper, and sharper question the repo has not run.
axiomatic.repo_overlap: No overlap with the off-limits topics (alternating-trace fiber, bounded-left-depth certificates, parity-checked survivor map, {1,4} wallpaper, column-band locks). Kinship with ARM7 only: ARM7's quadtree-DAG measurements double as evidence against 2D dyadic self-similarity, i.e., against 2-automaticity of the whole diagram, but ARM7 never frames automaticity, never touches the 1D column kernel, Christol, or FO-definability, and its contract (poly(log n) doubling state) is an algorithmic-compression goal, not a definability dichotomy. ARM8's ROBDD quotient concerns the arbitrary-input transfer function F_h, orthogonal to base-k self-similarity of the one-seed column. The proposed gap sits strictly outside both docs' stated conclusions and open edges.
axiomatic.verdict_rationale: Not novel-open: the framing (CA columns vs automaticity, plus the logic bridge) is an established, named line; Rowland-Yassawi posed and Marcovici-Stoll-Tahay answered the general nonlinear-column question, and the definability/decidability machinery (Büchi-Bruyère, Honkala, Sutner/Finkel, Jeandel-Theyssier) is textbook. Not closed: nothing in that line settles or dooms the Rule 30 instance; the ASY toolbox has never been aimed at it, arXiv has zero papers on the intersection, and both branches of the dichotomy carry prize consequences. The exact boundary: linear CA columns fully characterized; nonlinear nonautomatic columns exist by bespoke construction; no criterion, no kernel data, no definability statement for Rule 30's column. The open edge is the instance, with the caveat that the negative branch is provably harder than P1 itself, which caps expected yield.
axiomatic.candidate_first_experiment: Truncated 2-kernel census on N >= 2^20 center-column bits: for each level i <= 18, count distinct subsequences (c(2^i n + j))_n distinguished by a shared 256-bit window; report distinct-count per level and the induced Myhill-Nerode minimal-DFA state lower bound as window length doubles. Controls: Rule 90 and Rule 150 columns (automatic, kernels must saturate at O(1) — validation), seeded random column (full 2^i growth). Cheapest disconfirming test of the expected conclusion: Rule 30's counts saturating like Rule 90's instead of tracking the random control.
axiomatic.kill_condition_sketch: Two-level. Experiment kill (fires on a plausible negative of the expected outcome): Rule 30's truncated kernel count saturates at some level with count far below 2^i and stays saturated as both window length and N double — the non-automaticity expectation is disconfirmed; pivot to synthesizing the candidate DFA and testing it predictively on held-out bits (a survival there would refute the P3 conjecture, so this branch is not wasted). Direction kill (fires on the more plausible negative): kernel counts equal 2^i at every measurable level, indistinguishable from the random control, AND a finite audit of every method in the ASY 2021 catalogue shows its premise instantiated for A051023 is itself unproven and implies-or-equals P1 (e.g., superlinear factor complexity, non-rational letter frequency). Then the technique is a restatement funnel with no independent lever and is closed; the audit is finite and the empirical half runs in one night.

hydro.already_proved: Four things are settled. (1) Measure level: the uniform Bernoulli(1/2) measure is exactly invariant under Rule 30 because Rule 30 is surjective (Hedlund balance theorem; stated as the well-known special case in Kari-Taati). So the coarse-grained density answer is already known exactly and is stationary; mean-field and every finite order of Gutowitz-Victor-Knight local structure theory merely approximate this exact fixed point (the order-1 mean-field fixed point is exactly 1/2 and stable). (2) Conservation: Rule 30 provably has no nontrivial additive conserved quantity at any window order (Hattori-Takesue 1991 table; Baird-Fagin 2010 lists Rule 30 among rules "known to have no nontrivials"). (3) Rigorous deterministic-CA hydrodynamics exists, but only where a conserved density exists: Belitsky-Ferrari 2005 derive Burgers hydrodynamics for the number-conserving Rule 184; conservation is the engine of the proof. (4) Exact coarse-graining: Rule 30 admits no exact supercell coarse-graining for any supercell size N<=7 (Israeli-Goldenfeld 2006 for N<=4; Song-Grochow 2020 to N=7); whether it is inherently un-coarse-grainable is explicitly open. The newest continuum-limit paper (Chan-Lopez & Martin-Ruiz 2026) gets a rigorous PDE only for the symmetric Rule 22 and nothing formal for Rule 30's column.
hydro.open_gap: Within the assigned technique, no unexplored gap bears on the center column. The three genuinely open questions adjacent to it all exit the technique: (a) whether Rule 30 admits an exact coarse-graining at some supercell size N>=8 or is inherently un-coarse-grainable (open since Israeli-Goldenfeld 2006, exhausted to N=7 by Song-Grochow 2020); a referee can check that neither answer yields a center-column statement, since a valid projection is irreversible and discards precisely the fine-grained cell values c_t. (b) Randomization for Rule 30: Cesaro convergence of iterated non-uniform Bernoulli measures to uniform Bernoulli, proven only for algebraic/linear CA (Lind/Miyamoto/Pivato-Yassawi line, per Kari-Taati); open for Rule 30, but its initial data are measures with full support, not the Dirac measure on ...0001000..., so even a full randomization theorem says nothing about the prize problems. (c) Orbit equidistribution of the single-seed orbit's empirical measures, which would imply P2; this is P2 restated in ergodic language, has no literature, and is a symbolic-dynamics question, not a coarse-grained-density or PDE question. There is no fourth option: a density PDE needs a slow field, and Rule 30 provably has none.
hydro.proof_relevance: None plausible. The nominal target is P2's statement lim_{T->inf} (1/T) sum_{t<T} c_t = 1/2, but this technique cannot produce it even in principle: the coarse-grained density field is a spatial-average object whose exact measure-level value (1/2, from invariance of the uniform Bernoulli measure under the surjective Rule 30) is already a theorem, and that theorem yields zero progress on P2 because P2 is a temporal average along one column of one deterministic orbit from a Dirac initial condition. Bridging spatial coarse-grained density to the column's temporal average requires orbitwise spatio-temporal equidistribution of the single-seed orbit, a statement at least as strong as P2 that no hydrodynamic or PDE framework addresses. And the standard route to a rigorous hydrodynamic limit is foreclosed outright: such theorems transport conserved quantities, and Rule 30 provably has no nontrivial conserved quantity at any order. No leverage on P1 or P3 either (coarse-graining is irreversible, so it can neither certify aperiodicity of c_t nor lower-bound the cost of computing c_t).
hydro.feasibility: The empirical program is fully runnable overnight on one Apple Silicon Mac in Python: bit-packed NumPy simulation of the single-seed diagram to t ~ 10^5-10^6 with a sliding window; multi-scale coarse-grained density fields at supercell widths 2^3-2^10; fluctuation-scaling tests against the CLT w^{-1/2} prediction; sparse-regression (PDE-FIND style) fits of candidate PDEs on the deviation field; local-structure-theory block-probability iteration to order ~8. Exhaustive exact-projection search is feasible for N<=4 (2^16 binary projections), borderline at N=5 equal partitions (~3x10^8 candidates, doable bit-packed overnight), and out of reach at N>=6, where prior work already reports negative results anyway. The bind is not compute: every runnable artifact is an empirical fit or an approximation without error control, and none can be promoted to a formal statement about c_t.

hydro.verdict_rationale: The direction is doomed by four independent, literature-anchored obstructions. (1) No slow mode: hydrodynamic PDEs describe transport of conserved densities, and Rule 30 provably has no nontrivial additive conserved quantity at any order (Hattori-Takesue 1991; Baird-Fagin 2010 verbatim "known to have no nontrivials"); the one rigorous deterministic-ECA hydrodynamic limit in existence (Rule 184 -> Burgers, Belitsky-Ferrari 2005) runs entirely on number conservation, which Rule 30 lacks. (2) Nothing left to pin: the exact measure-level density is already a theorem (uniform Bernoulli invariant under the surjective Rule 30, Kari-Taati), so mean-field/LST/fitted PDEs can only re-approximate a known constant; the technique's entire output space collapses to "rho = 1/2 identically inside the cone", which is insensitive to everything P2 asks. (3) Wrong observable: P2 is a temporal average along one deterministic column from a Dirac initial condition; coarse-graining is a spatial-LLN operation that erases exactly that information, and the missing bridge (orbit equidistribution) is P2 itself in ergodic clothing, not a PDE statement. (4) Even the exact-projection version of "coarse-grain Rule 30" fails empirically at every searched scale (Israeli-Goldenfeld 2006; Song-Grochow 2020 to N=7), and the newest formal continuum-limit paper (Chan-Lopez & Martin-Ruiz, arXiv:2604.00165, 2026) achieves rigor only for the symmetric Rule 22, confirming that this lane, actively worked as recently as 2026, produces no center-column theorem. The assignment's warning condition ("find the edge past Gutowitz/mean-field or return closed") resolves to closed: the only open questions past that line are un-coarse-grainability and randomization, and neither is a density-PDE question nor a path to P1/P2/P3.
hydro.candidate_first_experiment: If this became an arm despite the verdict, the cheapest disconfirming test: simulate the single-seed diagram to t = 2x10^5; compute coarse density fields rho_w(x,tau) at supercell scales w = 8..1024 inside the light cone (excluding the regular left edge); test whether the deviation field rho_w - 1/2 (i) decays like w^{-1/2} consistent with pure CLT fluctuations and (ii) supports any cross-validated sparse-regression PDE whose residual improves with scale. One Python script, under an hour of CPU. Expected outcome per the literature: (i) holds, (ii) fails, i.e. the macroscopic field is the contentless rho = 1/2 and there is no hydrodynamic structure to model.
hydro.kill_condition_sketch: Kill if, across scales w = 8..1024, the in-cone coarse density is statistically indistinguishable from constant 1/2 with fluctuations scaling as w^{-1/2} (no coherent macroscopic mode beyond the left-edge boundary layer), and no fitted local PDE on the deviation field beats the trivial model rho = 1/2 under cross-validation with residuals decreasing as scale grows. This condition can genuinely fire on the plausible negative, and given the exact invariance of the uniform measure it is expected to fire; conversely a persistent scale-coherent deviation would falsify the doom argument and reopen the arm.

padic.already_proved: (i) Automata functions coincide with 1-Lipschitz (continuous) maps on Z_p, with a full ergodic/measure theory via van der Put series (Anashin school; Tyapaev for the dynamical framing). (ii) Finite-state = p-automatic reduced van der Put coefficients (Anashin 2012; Grigorchuk-Savchuk 2020 with explicit two-way algorithms). (iii) Spacetime diagrams of morphism CA on commutative monoids are k-automatic, and p-automatic sequences are exactly the columns of linear CA over F_p (Litow-Dumas / Rowland-Yassawi / Nesme); this line stops at algebraic rules and says nothing about Rule 30. (iv) Rule 30's SE diagonals are purely periodic with power-of-2 periods, at most doubling per diagonal (Rowland 2006 Lemma 2 + NKS p.871 bound). In 2-adic language, though no source says it this way: t -> R(t) (right-aligned row) extends uniquely to a 1-Lipschitz function R-hat: Z_2 -> Z_2 whose k-th digit layer is the k-th diagonal's periodic word; the center cell is the moving digit c(t) = digit_t(R(t)). (v) Ultimate periodicity of automatic sequences is decidable (Honkala 1986).
padic.open_gap: No published work applies the van der Put / 1-Lipschitz machinery to the TIME direction of any nonlinear CA spacetime. Concretely unoccupied (checked: "Rule 30"+2-adic/p-adic, van der Put+cellular automaton, center column+automatic all return nothing; OEIS A051023 carries no such comment): (a) the object R-hat itself, the 1-Lipschitz 2-adic extension of t -> right-aligned row, well-defined by Rowland 2006 but never constructed; (b) the dichotomy "is R-hat a finite automaton function?", equivalently by Anashin's criterion "is the reduced van der Put coefficient sequence, i.e. a finite-alphabet encoding of Rowland's nested diagonal-word family, 2-automatic?" — genuinely open, decidable-feeling, and unposed anywhere; (c) any rigidity theorem in non-archimedean analysis controlling the moving diagonal digit_t(f(t)) of a 1-Lipschitz f. Scoping caveat from a construction I verified by hand this session: a profile-level theorem is impossible — for any period profile matching Rule 30's one can build a 1-Lipschitz g with identical van der Put profile whose moving diagonal IS eventually periodic (each diagonal word meets the moving diagonal in exactly one position, which can be set freely and the rest of the word tuned to preserve exact period). So the open edge is strictly at coefficient-CONTENT level: automaticity or provable non-automaticity of the actual Rowland diagonal-word family, and content-aware moving-diagonal rigidity.
padic.proof_relevance: Branch 1 (conditional reduction): if R-hat is finite-state, then the center column c(t) = digit_t(R(t)) is 2-automatic — proof sketch: c(t) is the Mealy output after feeding binary(t) LSB-first then t+1-len(t) zeros; the state after binary(t) is a 2-automatic function of t, the zero-padding count enters only through (t - floor(log2 t)) mod (cycle period), and both t mod q and digit-length mod q are 2-automatic, so c is a finite combination of 2-automatic sequences. Then P1 becomes a Honkala-decidable check, and finite-state R-hat would compute c(t) in poly(log t) time, REFUTING P3's conjecture. Branch 2 (the expected, unconditional target): "R-hat is not a finite automaton function," provable in principle via Anashin's criterion by showing the reduced van der Put coefficients are not 2-automatic. This is a necessary consequence of P3's conjecture (it rules out one concrete family of radical shortcuts: no finite 2-adic transducer in the time variable computes the right half of Rule 30), and is a new formal theorem about the structure surrounding the center column — but it does NOT by itself prove P1, P2, or P3. The dream statement, "the center column is not 2-automatic," is strictly stronger than P1 (eventually periodic implies 2-automatic) and would need the missing moving-diagonal rigidity of (c).
padic.feasibility: Runnable overnight: bit-packed numpy Rule 30 keeping only the current row (t rows cost ~t^2/128 uint64 ops; t = 5e7 is roughly 1-2 h, memory ~6 MB), recording the trailing ~64 right-aligned digits per row. That confirms exact diagonal periods to k ~ 60-70 (periods grow like 2^(0.38k) per A094605, so k=64 needs t ~ 5e7), computes the reduced van der Put coefficients of R-hat truncated mod 2^m, and runs 2-kernel/Myhill-Nerode growth tests on the coefficient sequence (cheap). Cross-checks against the billion-bit center-column dataset (Wolfram Data Repository, Xiangdong Wen 2019) are cheap lookups. Not runnable: full-width simulation much beyond t ~ 1e8, hence periods of diagonals past k ~ 80 (2^30+) are out of reach, as is any brute-force attack on the center column itself.
padic.repo_overlap: None of the off-limits topics: this arm lives on the southeast diagonals / right-aligned rows in the TIME direction and their van der Put coefficients, not on traces, fibers, survivor maps, the wallpaper member, or column-band locks. It takes the settled SE-diagonal periodicity as input, same as the ground rules do. One adjacency to watch: it consumes the same Rowland 2006 nested-diagonal structure that Rowland-style column-band lock proofs use; the arm must stay on the 2-adic-in-t function and its coefficient automaticity, never drifting into spatial column-band arguments.
padic.verdict_rationale: The prior line is real and mature on both flanks: (1) automata = 1-Lipschitz maps on Z_p with a complete van der Put finite-state criterion (Anashin 2012; Grigorchuk-Savchuk 2020), and (2) automatic spacetime diagrams for algebraic CA, currently up to commutative-monoid morphisms (Rowland-Yassawi 2015; Nesme 2022-2026, v5 dated 2026-08-26). Its exact boundary: flank (1) has never been pointed at a CA spacetime, and flank (2) stops at morphism rules, excluding Rule 30 by rule type. Direct searches for Rule 30 + 2-adic surface only fuzzy-CA dynamics and p-adic-VALUED-state logic CA, a different object. The specific open edge past the boundary: construct R-hat (licensed by Rowland 2006 pure periodicity, never done), settle its finite-state status via Anashin's criterion, and pursue content-aware moving-diagonal rigidity. Not novel-open because the entire toolset and the licensing theorem are published and the contribution is their unperformed composition; not closed because my profile-level impossibility construction only kills the lazy version, while the coefficient-content question is genuinely unposed and both of its answers produce formal statements (one refutes P3's expectation and decides P1's status on that branch; the other is a new necessary-condition theorem for P3).
padic.candidate_first_experiment: One overnight run: (1) simulate to t ~ 1e7-5e7 with bit-packed numpy, extract SE diagonal words to k ~ 60, validate exact periods against A094605 (correctness gate); (2) encode the reduced van der Put coefficients of R-hat over a finite alphabet (coefficients mod 2^m, m = 8 and 16) and measure 2-kernel growth (number of distinct subsequences b(2^i t + j)) as a Myhill-Nerode lower bound on any Moore automaton generating them; (3) as a same-night control, instantiate the profile-matched counterexample g and confirm its kernel behaves qualitatively differently. Kernel saturation at some finite state count would flip the arm to the sensational finite-state branch, immediately testable against the billion-bit center-column dataset; unbounded kernel growth at the raw diagonal-word rate ~2^(0.38k) with no compression means Anashin's criterion certifies nothing automatic is present and only the (much harder) non-automaticity proof remains.
padic.kill_condition_sketch: Kill fires if BOTH: (a) the 2-kernel lower bound for the reduced van der Put coefficient sequence grows without saturation and tracks the trivial count of distinct diagonal words (~2^(0.38k)) through k = 40-60 with no substitution-like compression detectable (i.e., the coefficient sequence shows no more structure than the raw diagonals Rowland already described), and (b) the explicit profile-matched 1-Lipschitz counterexample with eventually periodic moving diagonal is written up cleanly, establishing that no theorem quantifying only over van der Put profiles can prove P1. Under (a)+(b) the 2-adic frame is demonstrably a relabeling of Rowland 2006 with no added leverage, and the arm closes; this can plausibly fire, since (b) is already constructible and (a) is the generic expectation for a chaotic rule.

anf.already_proved: Everything proven is at one iteration of the local rule: the 3-variable ANF (p XOR q XOR r XOR qr), nonlinearity 2, failure of first-order correlation immunity (Meier-Staffelbach 1991; Martin 2008 proves no nonlinear ECA rule is CI(1)), and best-affine-approximation agreement 3/4 enabling inversion (Koc-Apohan 1997). At two iterations there is only an exhaustive CI-preservation check for diameter-5 rules (Formenti et al. 2014). For f_t itself the literature has only empirics: minimal DNF term counts 3, 7, 17, 41, 102, 261 for t=1..6 (NKS pp. 618-619). Balancedness of every f_t under the uniform measure follows from left-permutivity (classical; restated as Chan-López Theorem 3), which is why P2 holds trivially for random initial conditions. Separately, the P1-adjacent line (Jen 1990, Kopra 2023) proves width-2 trace aperiodicity by symbolic dynamics, with the width-1 single-seed case explicitly open.
anf.open_gap: No published theorem gives, for general t, the algebraic degree, ANF monomial count, or maximal Walsh coefficient of the t-iterated Rule 30 center-bit function f_t on 2t+1 variables; no inductive lemma controls ANF growth under the overlapping-window composition (where variable sharing collapses degree: hand-check here gives deg f_2 = 3, not the naive 4, because cross terms like (cd)(de) = cde); and no work connects any such family-level statement to P1/P2/P3. Mariot's own 2024 survey lists the algebraic-degree investigation as future work in the PRG frame. The 2026 Chan-López paper works with row-support polynomials, a different object, and leaves all Rule 30 closed forms open. A referee can check novelty by searching for any proven statement of the form \"deg f_t = t+1\" or \"the ANF support of iterated Rule 30 grows like c^t\" or \"max |Walsh(f_t)| decays in t\": none exists. Candidate provable targets: (a) deg f_t = t+1 with a characterized top homogeneous layer satisfying a window-shift recursion (plausibly provable by induction through the OR-chain plus left-permutivity); (b) exponential ANF support growth calibrated against the NKS DNF counts; (c) decay of the maximal correlation with linear functions, upgrading Meier-Staffelbach's t=1 correlation 3/4 to an asymptotic correlation-immunity theorem for the family.
anf.proof_relevance: In principle this line can produce real theorems about the center-cell FUNCTION FAMILY: \"for all t, deg f_t = t+1 (or >= ct) and |ANF(f_t)| = 2^{Theta(t)}, and max_a |corr(f_t, <a,x>)| -> 0\". Tied to P3, such a theorem is a model-restricted lower bound: no o(t)-degree or 2^{o(t)}-sparse GF(2)-polynomial in the initial cells computes the general-IC center cell, ruling out one concrete class of radical shortcuts. It is NOT P3: degree lower bounds do not bound time (parity has full degree and linear-time circuits), and P3 concerns the single-seed instance, a single evaluation point about which family-level spectral facts say nothing. For P1: no known bridge; eventual periodicity is a statement about f_t evaluated at one fixed point, and the line that actually touches P1 (Jen/Kopra) runs through shift dynamics, not spectra. For P2: balancedness yields only the uniform-measure analogue, already classical. Honest summary: the strongest plausible formal output is a restricted-model P3-adjacent impossibility theorem plus unconditional structural lemmas; no plausible route to P1/P2 as posed without a currently nonexistent bridge from function-family structure to the single orbit.
anf.feasibility: Fully runnable. Exact ANF via bit-packed fast Mobius transform over the 2^{2t+1} truth table: t <= 13 is minutes in numpy (2^27 bits), t = 14-15 feasible overnight (2^29-2^31 bits, XOR-shift across axes on uint64 words, <= 256 MB). Full Walsh-Hadamard needs int32 accumulation: t <= 12-13 (2^27 entries, ~0.5-1 GB) overnight on one Apple Silicon Mac in Python/CPU. Not runnable: exact spectra beyond t ~ 13-14; sampled correlation estimates beyond that are statistical evidence and count for nothing under the ground rules, so the empirical phase is hard-capped at t ~ 14 and must aim at pattern-for-induction, not asymptotics.
anf.repo_overlap: None. The off-limits arms (alternating-trace fiber, bounded-left-depth exclusion certificates, parity-checked survivor map, {1,4} wallpaper member, column-band locks) and the falsified dead ends (prefix-OR latch, wedge descent, cascade descent, trace-anchored O(log t) propagation) are all trace/fiber constructions, not Boolean-function analysis of f_t. One flag: an unrefereed 2026 Wolfram Cloud notebook (Tigran Nersissian, \"Rule 30 Exact Binomial-Lucas Lifting...\") claims a one-sided ANF recursion yielding O(log n) evaluation, a cousin of the locally falsified trace-anchored O(log t) idea; treat as a red flag to distinguish from, not prior art.
anf.verdict_rationale: A genuine prior line exists and is exactly locatable: one-step ANF/Walsh properties of Rule 30 are fully settled and were weaponized (Meier-Staffelbach 1991, Koc-Apohan 1997, Martin 2008), iterated properties were touched exactly once and only to depth 2 for diameter-5 rules (Formenti et al. 2014), and the field's 2024 survey explicitly marks the algebraic-degree line as uninvestigated. The boundary is sharp: every proven statement stops at t = 1 (t = 2 for one exhaustive check), and the 2026 algebraic Rule 30 paper studies row polynomials, not f_t. Past that boundary lies a concrete, cheaply testable, plausibly provable open edge (exact degree law t+1, top-layer recursion, support growth, Walsh decay) that no one occupies. It is not novel-open because the technique, objects, and motivating attacks are all established; it is not closed because nothing in the literature settles or dooms the iterated-growth questions. The honest ceiling, which must be stated in any pre-registration: full success yields restricted-model P3-adjacent theorems and unconditional structure lemmas, with no existing bridge to P1/P2.
anf.candidate_first_experiment: Compute the exact ANF of f_t for t = 1..14 by bit-packed fast Mobius transform (and full Walsh spectra for t <= 12): record deg f_t, |ANF support|, the set of top-degree monomials, and max |Walsh coefficient|. Test three pre-registered laws before any lemma-hunting: deg f_t = t+1; top homogeneous layer satisfies a window-shift recursion in the right-side variables; max normalized correlation with linear functions decays from the known 1/2 at t = 1. Cross-check support counts against the NKS DNF sizes (3, 7, 17, 41, 102, 261) as an implementation sanity gate.
anf.kill_condition_sketch: Kill fires if any of: (a) deg f_t deviates from t+1 (and from every affine-in-t law) at some t <= 14; (b) the top-degree monomial set fails to satisfy any shift/window recursion by t = 12, so no induction hypothesis exists to prove; (c) max normalized Walsh coefficient plateaus (stays >= 2^-4 across t = 8..12 with no decreasing trend), killing the asymptotic-correlation-immunity target. Firing (a)+(b) leaves no provable structural lemma and closes the arm; these are plausible negatives because the degree collapse that makes deg f_2 = 3 depends on delicate cancellations that need not stay regular.

ergodic.technique: Ergodic theory / measure rigidity: classify jointly (shift, Rule 30)-invariant measures on {0,1}^Z; treat P2 as equidistribution of the single-seed orbit's empirical measures toward uniform Bernoulli

closest_prior_work.citation: B. Host, A. Maass, S. Martinez, "Uniform Bernoulli measure in dynamics of permutative cellular automata with algebraic local rules", Discrete Contin. Dyn. Syst. 9(6):1423-1446 (2003). https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/canadian-journal-of-mathematics/article/automaticity-and-invariant-measures-of-linear-cellular-automata/4756BA06195903E4075BFA34195A406E (cited there); restated verbatim in Kari-Taati Example 46
closest_prior_work.what_it_shows: For the XOR CA with neighborhood {0,1} (and algebraic permutive relatives), the uniform Bernoulli measure is the ONLY shift-ergodic probability measure that is CA-invariant and of positive entropy. This is the exact template statement the technique wants for Rule 30, proved only in the algebraic case.

closest_prior_work.citation: M. Pivato, "Invariant measures for bipermutative cellular automata", Discrete Contin. Dyn. Syst. 12(4):723-736 (2005). https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0306211
closest_prior_work.what_it_shows: Rigidity extended beyond group-algebraic rules to bipermutative right-sided nearest-neighbor CA via quasigroup structure (plus: any invariant measure makes F a.e. constant-to-1). Bipermutivity is essential; Rule 30 is left-permutive but not right-permutive, so excluded.

closest_prior_work.citation: M. Sablik, "Measure rigidity for algebraic bipermutative cellular automata", Ergodic Theory Dynam. Systems 27(6) (2007); arXiv:math/0510564. https://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/~msablik/article/2007-etds.pdf
closest_prior_work.what_it_shows: Conditions forcing a (shift, CA)-invariant measure to be Haar on a closed shift-invariant subgroup, for algebraic bipermutative CA. Again both hypotheses (algebraic, bipermutative) fail for Rule 30.

closest_prior_work.citation: J. Kari, S. Taati, "Statistical Mechanics of Surjective Cellular Automata", J. Stat. Phys. 160(5):1198-1243 (2015); arXiv:1311.2319 (read verbatim from the PDF this session)
closest_prior_work.what_it_shows: Theorem 47 / Corollary 48: a strongly transitive CA conserves no non-trivial Hamiltonian and preserves no regular Gibbs measure other than maximum-entropy ones. Example 46 caveat: even for XOR there are many non-Gibbs jointly invariant measures (Dirac at 0^Z, atomic measures on jointly periodic orbits), so rigidity needs entropy/ergodicity hypotheses. Application to Rule 30 would need Rule 30's strong transitivity, which no retrieved source establishes, and even then only the Gibbs class is excluded.

closest_prior_work.citation: B. Hellouin de Menibus, V. Salo, G. Theyssier, "Characterizing Asymptotic Randomization in Abelian Cellular Automata", arXiv:1703.07289 (2017), published in Ergodic Theory Dynam. Systems. https://arxiv.org/abs/1703.07289
closest_prior_work.what_it_shows: Complete characterization of Cesaro-mean randomization (F^t mu -> uniform) for abelian CA: randomizes iff no soliton. The randomization program is fully algebraic to date; initial measures must be non-atomic (Bernoulli/ergodic classes), never a Dirac at a single configuration like the single seed.

closest_prior_work.citation: B. Hellouin de Menibus, V. Salo, I. Torma, "Symbol Frequencies in Surjective Cellular Automata", arXiv:2504.06058 (2025), AUTOMATA 2025, LNCS (doi 10.1007/978-3-032-01570-9_11). https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.06058
closest_prior_work.what_it_shows: For general surjective CA, weak-* limit points of iterated measures can misbehave (full support can be lost from an ergodic full-support start). Current frontier for non-algebraic surjective CA measure dynamics; provides preimage symbol-frequency tools but no rigidity and no Rule 30 statement.

closest_prior_work.citation: M. Tal, "On a Constraint on Invariant Measures of Certain Cellular Automata", arXiv:2604.10124 (submitted 2026-04-11)
closest_prior_work.what_it_shows: Newest entry in the line (April 2026): a conditional-uniformity constraint on invariant measures, still only for BI-permutative CA (group alphabets). Confirms the active frontier has not crossed the bipermutivity boundary toward Rule 30.

closest_prior_work.citation: R. Kleveland, "Mixing properties of one-dimensional cellular automata", Proc. Amer. Math. Soc. 125(6):1755-1766 (1997)
closest_prior_work.what_it_shows: Leftmost- and rightmost-permutive CA are strongly mixing w.r.t. uniform product measure; covers Rule 30. So (uniform, Rule 30) is a strongly mixing positive-entropy jointly invariant measure, which is what makes the equidistribution target imply P1 as well as P2.

closest_prior_work.citation: D. Lind, "Applications of ergodic theory and sofic systems to cellular automata", Physica D 10(1-2):36-44 (1984). https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/016727898490246X
closest_prior_work.what_it_shows: The founding randomization result: rule 90 Cesaro-randomizes Bernoulli initial measures, via Fourier analysis on the group structure. Method intrinsically additive/algebraic.

closest_prior_work.citation: B. Host, "Nombres normaux, entropie, translations", Israel J. Math. 91:419-428 (1995). https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/BF02761660
closest_prior_work.what_it_shows: The x2-x3 analogue of the wanted bridge: positive-entropy invariance gives normality for mu-ALMOST EVERY point, never for a specified point (e.g. 1/3). Structural precedent that rigidity theorems do not reach individual orbits, which is exactly the P2 obstruction here.

closest_prior_work.citation: M. Pivato, "Ergodic theory of cellular automata", Encyclopedia of Complexity and Systems Science, Springer (2009), pp. 2980-3015; also Int. J. General Systems 41(6) (2012). https://link.springer.com/rwe/10.1007/978-1-4939-8700-9_178
closest_prior_work.what_it_shows: Survey explicitly listing the characterization of (shift, CA)-invariant measures as an open problem, with rigidity understood only under compatible algebraic structure.

ergodic.already_proved: Uniform Bernoulli IS jointly (shift, Rule 30)-invariant (balance property of surjective CA; Kari-Taati sec. 4.2) and (uniform, Rule 30) is strongly mixing (Kleveland 1997). Full rigidity, i.e. "uniform is the unique shift-ergodic positive-entropy CA-invariant measure", is proved ONLY under bipermutivity and/or algebraic local rules (Host-Maass-Martinez 2003 for XOR-type; Pivato 2005 quasigroup bipermutative; Sablik 2007 algebraic bipermutative; Tal 2026 still bipermutative). For merely surjective chaotic CA, Kari-Taati Cor. 48 excludes non-max-entropy REGULAR GIBBS invariant measures for strongly transitive CA, with the explicit caveat (their Example 46) that abundant non-Gibbs jointly invariant measures always exist (Dirac at 0^Z, atomic on jointly periodic orbits). Randomization (Cesaro convergence of F^t mu to uniform) is characterized for abelian CA only (Hellouin de Menibus-Salo-Theyssier 2017) and always assumes non-atomic initial measures.
ergodic.open_gap: Two nested gaps, both checkable by literature absence. (G1) No theorem or counterexample exists on jointly invariant measures of ANY left-permutive, non-right-closing, non-algebraic CA; in particular "is uniform Bernoulli the unique shift-ergodic positive-entropy (shift, Rule 30)-invariant measure?" appears in no paper (the XOR analogue is HMM 2003; Pivato's 2009 survey lists the general problem as open; the April 2026 frontier, Tal arXiv:2604.10124, is still bipermutative). Even the finite sub-question "does Rule 30 admit a non-uniform (shift,F)-invariant Markov measure of small memory?" is unpublished, and Rule 30's strong transitivity (which via Kari-Taati Cor. 48 would settle the Gibbs part) is not established in any retrieved source. (G2) No published work connects CA measure rigidity to a single-orbit statement: weak-* limits of the empirical measures (1/N) sum_{t<N} delta_{F^t x0} of the single-seed orbit are automatically F-invariant but NOT automatically shift-invariant (the space-time diagram has a distinguished origin and a regular left region), and the zero-entropy jointly invariant measure delta_{0^Z} cannot be excluded from the limit set without independently lower-bounding the density of 1s in the center column. The x2-x3 precedent (Rudolph-type rigidity plus Host 1995 gives only a.e. normality, never normality of 1/3) shows G2 is the deep part and is untouched for CA.
ergodic.proof_relevance: Formal target: "every weak-* limit point of (1/N) sum_{t<N} delta_{F^t x0} equals the uniform Bernoulli measure", for x0 the single-1 configuration. This immediately gives P2: the frequency of the cylinder [1] at coordinate 0 along the orbit converges to 1/2, i.e. the limiting center-column density exists and equals 1/2. Combined with Kleveland's strong mixing of (uniform, Rule 30), the same statement forces center-column time-autocorrelations (empirical measure of [1]_0 intersect F^{-s}[1]_0) to converge to 1/4 for every lag s, which is incompatible with eventual periodicity, yielding P1. A rigidity theorem "uniform is the unique positive-entropy shift-ergodic jointly invariant measure for Rule 30" would reduce this target to proving (a) shift-invariance and (b) non-degeneracy (positive entropy / no mass on the zero-entropy stratum, in particular not delta_{0^Z}) of empirical limits; both are open and (b) is itself P2-adjacent. No plausible route to P3.
ergodic.feasibility: Runnable overnight: (1) exact symbolic search for (shift,F)-invariant Markov measures of memory 1-3 for Rule 30: block probabilities of the image of a Markov measure under a radius-1 CA are exact finite transfer sums; setting image = original on all blocks up to length ~12 gives a small polynomial system in the transition parameters, solvable in sympy/rational arithmetic in hours; this is a theorem-shaped finite computation (a per-class exclusion or a counterexample), not statistics. (2) bit-packed numpy Rule 30 from the single seed for 10^5-10^6 rows (about 10^10 cell updates, about 10^8 word ops packed), collecting k-block frequencies (k up to about 16) of the center column and of columns at fixed offsets, testing convergence toward uniform and spatial stationarity of window statistics (the shift-invariance obstruction (a), made quantitative). NOT runnable: anything bearing on the rigidity proof itself or the generic-points bridge; and no amount of sampling tests P2 (statistical randomness evidence proves nothing and is claimed as nothing).
ergodic.repo_overlap: None with the off-limits list (alternating-trace fiber, bounded-left-depth exclusion certificates, parity-checked survivor map, {1,4} wallpaper member, column-band locks). This technique works at the level of global measures on {0,1}^Z, not trace fibers. One forward-looking seam: the repo's zero-trace fiber classification (prefix-OR) describes conditional structure over a trace, which a future conditional-measure/disintegration argument could consume, but nothing proposed here re-derives or competes with it.
ergodic.verdict_rationale: A mature, still-active prior line (Lind 1984 through Tal, April 2026) owns invariant-measure rigidity and randomization for CA, so this is not novel-open; but every positive theorem stops at an exactly nameable boundary, bipermutivity/algebraicity for uniqueness and the regular-Gibbs class for chaotic surjective CA, and Rule 30 sits strictly outside both (left-permutive only, non-algebraic). Nothing closes the direction either: no counterexample measure is known for Rule 30, and the field's own surveys state the classification problem as open. The two-part open edge is precise: (G1) any invariant-measure statement for a merely left-permutive non-algebraic CA, starting with the finite Markov-measure question, and (G2) the generic-points bridge from rigidity to the single-seed orbit, which has no CA analogue anywhere and is known-hard by the x2-x3 normality precedent. Honest expectation management: even total success on G1 leaves G2, which is the ergodic-theory analogue of proving 1/3 is normal, so this is a long-horizon program, not a prize shortcut.
ergodic.candidate_first_experiment: Exact memory-1 then memory-2 invariant-Markov search: parametrize shift-invariant Markov measures on {0,1}^Z, compute Rule 30 image block probabilities exactly by transfer sums, impose invariance on all blocks up to length 12, solve the resulting polynomial system in rational/symbolic arithmetic (hours on CPU). Outcome A (only uniform among positive-entropy solutions): first published exclusion evidence for the uniqueness conjecture, extendable memory by memory. Outcome B (a non-uniform solution): the rigidity route dies same-day. Follow with the overnight 10^5-10^6-row empirical block-frequency and spatial-stationarity scan of the single-seed center window to quantify obstruction (a).
ergodic.kill_condition_sketch: Kill fires if the exact search (memory up to 3, blocks up to length 12, exact arithmetic) produces a non-uniform positive-entropy (shift, Rule 30)-invariant Markov measure whose invariance verifies exactly; this is a plausible negative given Kari-Taati Example 46 shows non-Gibbs invariant measures abound even for XOR, and it would falsify the uniqueness conjecture the whole program rests on. Secondary kill on the equidistribution formulation: center-column k-block empirical frequencies (k=12-16) that remain outside the exact-uniform prediction by a persistent, N-stable margin as N grows through 10^5-10^6 rows, i.e. the deviation does not shrink like N^{-1/2}, killing "empirical limits = uniform Bernoulli" as the formal target (the weaker density-only version of P2 could survive it).
